note: Vectors for the members of `swarma-grant/4` (LIP-0020 section 11). Each vector is the signed form of a grant; `signed_form_hex` is the vector, and `signed_form`, where it is given, only shows the same octets. In the groups `valid`, `invalid` and `compound`, `expect` is `ok` or the first refusal of the pipeline of a signed object (W9.1 with W11.8 to W11.10). That outcome is the same for a reader that judges the proposal points of W11.10 and for one that does not. A vector with `context.parent` is read with that vector as the parent that the reader already read; `context.reference` is an identifier that another object states for the grant. A refused vector of `invalid` holds one defect and names a valid neighbour that differs from it in that defect: in one member of the payload, in octets outside the payload, or in the context. Where the defect is a property of the parent, the child names another parent, and its member `parent` and the context change together. The vectors of `no_neighbour` name none. Unless its claim says otherwise, the signature of a refused vector is valid for the octets shown. A vector of `compound` holds several defects on purpose and has no neighbour; the statement of one defect does not cover it. A vector of `undetermined` is a parent that breaks one proposal point of W11.10, named in `judged`, and nothing else: the witness key hash form of `script` or of `stop.script`, or a placement point of rule 8. Such a point is an addition of a draft and binds no reader until it is accepted. The vector passes steps 1 to 8 of the pipeline, and `outcomes` lists the two results of step 9: `ok` for a reader that does not judge the point, and GRANT_DELEGATE for a reader that does (W11.10). A checker refuses every other code. The presence of `stop`, the last index of a run of stop coins and a stop coin of its own for each row are no proposal points: every reader judges them, and their vectors stand in `invalid`. `not_exercised` lists the refusal codes that section 11 names and no vector of this file exercises, each with the reason and with the place where it is exercised. The file was computed by one implementation, tools/grantv4/grantv4.py, whose reader also checked it. An independent implementation recomputes, from `signed_form_hex` and `context` alone, the outcome of every vector of `valid`, `invalid` and `compound`, for a vector of `undetermined` that it passes steps 1 to 8 and gives one of its two outcomes, and for a valid vector its typed digest, its identifier, its content address, its signature under the key of the place and the script of its seal key. Keys are public test scalars and belong to nobody; signatures are made by the default signing algorithm of BIP-340 with the stated auxiliary randomness. No vector reads a chain: nothing here shows that a name, a coin, a seal or a block exists.

base.note: The primitives below are not repeated here. These vectors rest on them.

uses: the canonical, integer, signature and key cases of its inventory
laboratory.changes: `memberless-type-0` expects WIRE_TYPE for a grant that holds `type` alone. With members that expectation no longer holds, and the step depends on how the case presents the octets, which this file does not verify. A payload of `type` alone inside a signed form, as in grant-i-05, now refuses as WIRE_MEMBER at step 4 (W3.2). The bare octets `{"type":"swarma-grant/4"}` presented as a signed form refuse as WIRE_MEMBER at step 2 (W5.3), as they did before the grant had members.

parameters.placeholders: Every transaction id and the recent block are the SHA-256 of an ASCII label and name no transaction and no block. Names, action names and the kinds, resources, units and periods of limits are placeholders: no registry assigns them.

not_exercised.why: The pipeline of W11.8 never reports it. It is a check of an admission, which reads stated facts of a chain beside the octets of grants, and this file models no such fact and states results of the pipeline alone. The pipeline reads an `ordinal` of any value of its form; the ordinal is held against the rows of the parent at admission (LIP-0026 R2.1, R8.8).

The same grant to a recipient by name: the name and its owner key, and no request key.

A parent with two groups and nine rows. The first group names a certifier and has two ranges with their stop coins; the second states that it has no certifier and names the class of the issuer's own landlord. The pool of 380 is exactly 5 rows of 60 and 4 rows of 20.
A parent that pins no notary: one group without a certifier whose recipient is an exact name, with no limit and therefore no pool.
A child of grant-v-03 for the row of ordinal 1, signed by the delegation key of its parent. Its seal key is the child-seal key of the parent.
The payload of grant-v-01 signed with other auxiliary randomness: another signature and another content address, the same identifier.
A grant with an empty action set and no limit. It is well formed and authorizes nothing.

A parent whose signed form has exactly 65536 octets: 16 groups of 16 ranges, a range of 4096 coins, a range whose last coin has the index 4294967295, a class of 78 landlords, and an own limit whose resource is a filler that brings the size to the bound.
grant-v-01 with a reference that states its identifier.

The parent of grant-v-03 without a child-seal key. The document is well formed. Under LIP-0014 CS1 it is unusable as a parent: every child of it refuses as CHILD_SEAL_KEY at its admission, which is no step of this pipeline.

The parent of grant-v-03 at three largest counts: four notaries, 16 groups, and 16 ranges in its second group. Each of the 14 further groups has one row for an exact name, without a certifier and without a limit. The rows sum to 680, 5 of 60 and 19 of 20, and the pool of 700 leaves room for one more row of 20.
